Since sub-surface utilities will not be affected by the plan, street surfaces will not be disrupted by the planned project activity. The street surface of Front Street (between the curbs) is maintained by the State. Since it is part of the highway system, it receives little attention under the plan. Penn Street, as indicated by appendix I, will be reinforced and reconstructed in a number of areas. Small areas of street surface will also be reconstructed on McLay and Peffer Streets.
4. Sidewalk, Curb, Alleyway and Tree Improvement
As indicated by appendix I, a large percentage of the project's sidewalks, curbs and alleyways will be improved. The concrete sidewalks, depreciated by either time or the effects of flooding, will be reconstructed where indicated. Brick sidewalks in need of repair will be repaired in lieu of replacement with concrete. Project residents are proud of their brick sidewalks and prefer this treatment.
Project curbs, depending on type (granite or concrete) will be replaced or reset sidewalk. Areas where tree openings occur, will be repaired to allow for tree root expansion. New trees will be planted to replace missing trees or trees damaged by the flooding. Trees of medium size, selected for flood plain areas will be used: Red Maple, Nyssa, Planetree, and Bausman Elm. Areas not subject to frequent flooding will receive Red Oaks, Scarlet Oaks and Lindens.
Nearly all of the backyard alleyways in the residential portions of the project will be removed and replaced with a 4" concrete walk on a 4" base of crushed stone.
5. Parking Improvement
Parking spaces, or bays, will be improved in 5 areas throughout the project; these will compliment the areas of decreased residential land use. These areas will be paved and will also be equipped with lighting.
